fit_spin_aero — DRIVE ball op

• Data kinds: signal × points × table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.fit_spin_aero(t, p, bp: 'dict', *, omega0=None, fit_cl: 'bool' = False, omega_max: 'float' = 1000.0, iters: 'int' = 25, dt: 'float' = 0.001) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import ballistics; ballistics.fit_spin_aero(t, p, bp: 'dict', *, omega0=None, fit_cl: 'bool' = False, omega_max: 'float' = 1000.0, iters: 'int' = 25, dt: 'float' = 0.001) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("fit_spin_aero"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Reads drag and spin together (fit_spin with a free C_d): fits the drag + Magnus equations of motion to a trajectory (t_i, p_i) (an interval without bounces) with the 10 parameters (p₀, v₀, ω, C_d) by Levenberg–Marquardt (fit_cl=True frees the lift coefficient scale κ too, for 11 parameters).

The model C_d is a constant (no Re dependence is fitted); the lift is the spin-ratio empirical formula C_L = κ·S/(1 + 2S) (S = rω/|v|) with the scale κ at 1 by default. ★A bp with a numeric (constant) C_L is rejected (ValueError): the Magnus force of a constant C_L has a magnitude independent of ω, so the |ω| column vanishes and the spin magnitude cannot be read even in principle (measured: ω stays at 0).

What cannot be read is reported in the return value: drag is along −v and Magnus along ω × v (perpendicular to v), so the force directions separate orthogonally, but (a) with a short flight in which the speed hardly drops, C_d is entangled with v₀, (b) ω and the lift scale κ are degenerate (where S is small, C_L ≈ κS, so the force fixes only the product κ·ω), and (c) the component of ω parallel to v produces no force. These show up in cond (condition number of the scaled Jacobian), corr (correlation matrix of the estimates, in the order of param_names), cov_unit (covariance of the estimates per 1 m of position noise = the linearised Cramér–Rao bound; multiply by σ² for noise σ [m]), corr_cd_omega (correlation of C_d with the magnitude of ω⊥), corr_cd_v0 (correlation of C_d with the magnitude of the initial velocity), omega_axial_std_unit (standard deviation of the component of ω parallel to v, per 1 m of noise) and omega_perp_std_unit (standard deviation of each of the two perpendicular components of ω). Return value {"p0", "v0", "omega", "omega_perp", "cd", "cl_scale", "rms", "cond", "corr", "param_names", "cov_unit", "corr_cd_omega", "corr_cd_v0", "omega_axial_std_unit", "omega_perp_std_unit", "iters", "t0", "at_bound"}. A trajectory made with the same model is recovered to 1e-6 (gate). ★If the world is a different model (C_d depends on Re, C_L has a dip), the constant-fitted C_d, ω and C_L become effective values over the interval and are biased (the bias is measured in the PoC). omega_max is the same as in fit_spin (upper bound on the spin magnitude). Convergence is slow when omega0 is far from the truth, the trajectory is short or fit_cl=True, and some samples do not reach iters on the flat valley (if the returned iters equals the argument, the run was cut off).

Limits: with fit_cl=True the |ω| and κ columns are nearly parallel (cond large, corr ≈ ±1) — read ω from the ball's pattern (balltrack.spin_from_markers) and take the lift scale from the trajectory instead (fit_aero with ω known). A constant-C_L bp and fewer than 12 samples raise ValueError.
